answer: Divergent Route Attestation. Each identity must periodically submit routing traces over a fixed graph whose edges pass through a unique dune checkpoint tied to a hidden per-identity offset. Honest agents diverge naturally; clones sharing an origin collapse onto identical traces and get flagged at the quartz verification step. A solver must forge distinct vertex paths per clone, costing roughly O(k log k) extra trace generation and a fresh offset acquisition for every identity, so scaling clones multiplies compute rather than amortizing it.
